feed.rights: Explanations and summaries are generated by AI from the original text. Dates, rates and amounts are checked against the source, but errors are still possible, so always rely on the original. Nothing here is legal, tax or investment advice.

entry.title: Efficient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges: Hash-based proof verification on Bitcoin
entry.summary: Toward Eﬃcient Post-Quantum Bitcoin Bridges IACR ePrint · Nov 12, 2026This paper addresses BitVM-style protocols, which verify succinct proofs on Bitcoin by garbling a proof verifier off-chain. It proposes a post-quantum alternative using a hash-based STARK verifier fed with hash-based one-time keys, avoiding number-theoretic assumptions. The authors compile a complete verifier for WHIR-based STARK proofs from Ziren into a Boolean circuit and report circuit costs for the final recursive WHIR-proof verifier. They also measure the total virtual size of the transactions publishing the input with translated Winternitz keys, reporting 4.26 million virtual bytes for one key set.

entry.title: Cortex-FL: An Agent-Based System for Coordinating Federated Learning Collaboration
entry.summary: Cortex-FL: Agent-Mediated Collaboration for Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents Cortex-FL, a federated learning system in which agents handle collaboration. Users describe learning goals in natural language, and agents turn them into shared tasks, find collaborators, and negotiate participation agreements. Owners keep control of their local data, computation, and financial commitments. A four-node deployment demonstrates the full workflow, from collaboration formation through contract-governed training and model delivery to x402 settlement on a blockchain testnet.

entry.title: Omakase: Congestion control for blockchain transaction execution via conflict-graph integration
entry.summary: Omakase: Execution Congestion Control through Conflict-Graph Integration in Multi-Proposer Blockchain arXiv · Nov 13, 2026This paper presents Omakase, a parallel execution framework for multi-proposer blockchains where transaction execution is the main bottleneck. Replicas pre-execute their own proposed blocks on idle cores, build per-block conflict graphs, and integrate them across a round with a greedy scheduler. A graph-aware optimistic concurrency control executor then runs the integrated graph in dependency order. On 15,000 Ethereum mainnet blocks and synthetic workloads, it achieves a 2.47x speedup over sequential execution and more stable throughput under high contention.

entry.title: Verifiable Settlement and Pricing for Local Energy Markets on Hyperledger Besu
entry.summary: Verifiable Settlement and Pricing for Local Energy Markets: Architecture and Deployment on Hyperledger Besu arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper implements privacy-preserving local electricity trading on a Hyperledger Besu network with QBFT consensus, using an automated market maker to set prices. Individual electricity positions stay off-chain, while only aggregate supply and demand are published, and smart contracts compute prices every fifteen minutes. Poseidon2 commitments and UltraHonk zero-knowledge proofs generated from Noir circuits verify aggregation, payments, and daily balance updates. In a ten-household simulation, local trading covered 34.4% of demand and reduced grid-only costs by 30.5% under assumed tariffs.

entry.title: Cost of force-closing a Lightning channel: analysis of 974,000 channel closes, 2018–2026
entry.summary: What Does It Cost to Force-Close a Lightning Channel? Evidence from 974,000 Channel Closes, 2018-2026 arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper traces 973,581 Lightning Network channel closes from January 2018 to October 2026 on-chain and cross-checks 698,476 public closes with a separate chain index. It finds that fee spikes did not produce a wave of force closes. Force closes cost two to six times as much in fees as cooperative closes. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors measure force-close costs across fee regimes using 973,581 channel closes, informing zero-fee commitment and anchor-output design decisions.

entry.title: Blockchain reward systems for federated learning and the privacy-fairness tradeoff
entry.summary: Tokenized Reward Systems for Federated Learning: The Privacy vs. Fairness Tradeoff arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper designs and tests two Solidity smart contracts that distribute rewards in federated learning, one based on a public quality score and one that hides scores using a zero-knowledge proof. Experiments on MNIST with Sybil attacks, zero-gradient updates, and random noise show that the privacy-preserving version is less robust. Adversaries capture roughly double the average reward, and honest contributors can be fully excluded in later training stages.

entry.title: A systematic survey of design choices in Tendermint BFT consensus
entry.summary: SoK: Design Choices in Tendermint BFT Consensus arXiv · Nov 12, 2026This paper surveys the Tendermint Byzantine fault-tolerant consensus protocol and the research that proposes changes to it. It describes the baseline protocol by its design choices, such as vote dissemination and proposer rotation, and classifies each work by the choice it modifies and the properties it strengthens or weakens. The surveyed solutions are grouped into three concerns: performance, validator accountability, and protection of exploitable information. The authors also identify recurring strategies and pose open questions for future work.

entry.title: AraCrypto-ML: A Multi-Label Corpus of Arabic Facebook Cryptocurrency Posts by Communicative Function
entry.summary: AraCrypto-ML: A Multi-Label Corpus of Communicative Functions in Arabic Facebook Cryptocurrency Discourse arXiv · Nov 11, 2026This paper introduces AraCrypto-ML, a corpus of 10,000 multi-label annotated Arabic Facebook posts about cryptocurrency from 2014 to 2024, drawn from 2,898 public pages. Posts are labelled into six functional categories using the Fanar-2-27B model under a prompt-only protocol. The authors validate 1,000 posts against adjudicated gold labels and apply Rogan-Gladen calibration to correct labelling bias. Reaction patterns vary markedly across functions, with Love dominating Educational and Promotional posts and Haha most common on Skeptical-Warning posts.

entry.title: CuEVM: Scaling Smart Contract Execution on GPUs
entry.summary: CuEVM: Scaling Smart Contract Execution on GPUs arXiv · Nov 11, 2026Ethereum smart contracts process transactions worth billions of dollars daily, but the Ethereum Virtual Machine executes them sequentially, creating a performance bottleneck. This paper presents CuEVM, a GPU-native and semantically complete EVM execution engine that treats transaction execution as a massively parallel data processing problem. It passes 100% of the Ethereum VMTests and 96.2% of the full execution-test suite, and executes over 8 million ERC-20 transfers per second on a single commodity GPU. The authors also built CuEVM-fuzz, a smart contract fuzzer on top of CuEVM, which achieves over a million end-to-end executions per second.

entry.title: TxBench: A Benchmark of Attack Transactions and Evidence-Backed Negatives on Seven EVM Chains
entry.summary: TxBench: Verifying Public Incident Data to Benchmark Smart-Contract Attack Detectors arXiv · Nov 3, 2026TxBench is a benchmark for testing detectors of malicious smart-contract transactions, covering seven EVM chains. Its attack transactions come from cited incidents in BlockSec's library and the EVM Hack Registry, filtered by a five-step pipeline that rebuilds each transaction's execution, and its negatives are ordinary chain transactions confirmed as legitimate. Of 1,850 cited transactions, 1,012 attacks from 602 incidents were accepted. Four zero-shot LLMs were precise but detected at most 0.43 of the attacks and no key compromises. ★★★★ Notable: The authors present a benchmark of EVM attack transactions labeled by their own execution, with evidence-backed negatives; the summary reports 1,012 accepted attacks from 1,850 cited transactions, che Correction Nov 13, 2026: Moved from "Cryptography & Security" to "Crypto & Blockchain"

entry.title: Revisiting Fiat-Shamir Zero-Knowledge Proofs and Signatures Built on Seed-Friendly Sigma Protocols
entry.summary: Revisiting Fiat-Shamir NIZKPs and Signatures from Seed-Friendly Sigma Protocols IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies Fiat-Shamir non-interactive zero-knowledge proofs built from seed-friendly sigma protocols. The authors show that fixed-weight parallel repetition and seed-tree compression improve both proof compactness and security. When prover randomness comes from a salted seed tree interacting with a random oracle, the standard Fiat-Shamir compilation is straight-line extractable in the classical random-oracle model. ★★★★ Notable: The authors show fixed-weight repetition and seed-tree compression also improve security, giving straight-line extractable Fiat-Shamir NIZKPs with formal proofs and multi-proof zero knowledge, relevan

entry.title: DetTreeChain: A Ledger That Produces Blocks in Parallel on a Tree with Bounded Lane Divergence
entry.summary: DetTreeChain: Parallel Block Production on an N-ary Block Tree with Bounded Lane Divergence IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents DetTreeChain, a blockchain ledger in which up to N blocks are produced in parallel and arranged in an N-ary tree without later merging or reordering. Transactions are routed to lanes by a hash of the locking scripts they spend, so blocks in different lanes do not conflict. In a Rust prototype and in simulation, the multi-lane design wasted less work than a single chain at the same block rate.

entry.title: Adaptively Secure Batched Identity-Based Encryption from Static Assumptions
entry.summary: Adaptively Secure (Threshold) Batched IBE from Static Assumptions IACR ePrint · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents the first adaptively secure batched identity-based encryption scheme based on static assumptions. Its ciphertexts, digests, and batch keys each consist of a constant number of group elements, independent of batch size, and it supports exponential identity and epoch spaces. The authors also give a threshold version and translate the scheme to prime-order bilinear groups under the static MDDH assumption. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report the first adaptively secure batched IBE from static assumptions, avoiding q-type assumptions and random oracles, with a threshold variant.

entry.title: Undine: A Distributed Extendable Merkle Tree Store with Private Lookups
entry.summary: Undine: Distributed Extendable Merkle Tree Storage with Private Retrieval and Efficient Reconfiguration IACR ePrint · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents Undine, a scheme for storing a growing Merkle tree across independent servers while letting clients retrieve entries without revealing which one they open. It combines a linearly encoded distributed tree with a private information retrieval protocol over those fragments, and supports authenticated updates and appends. The authors also evaluate UndineLog, an append-only implementation combined with YPIR.

entry.title: Testing whether Bitcoin's long-run price growth follows a power-law trend
entry.summary: Deceleration without identification: testing a power-law trend in Bitcoin prices under persistent noise arXiv · Nov 10, 2026The paper examines whether Bitcoin's price since its first block follows a power-law trend in time. Using fifteen years of weekly prices, the authors apply a pre-declared test built on low-frequency averages, calibrated over a specified family of persistent deviations. Constant drift is rejected, while a log-age coefficient of 5.7, close to the published exponent, is not rejected. The authors note the rejection does not hold if persistence beyond a random walk is allowed, and a Gompertz curve with a ceiling fits about as well, so reversion to trend cannot be decided.

entry.title: Study of how faster blockchain block speeds affect arbitrage and liquidity provision
entry.summary: Optimal Trading Speed on Blockchain arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper examines how block speed on blockchain-based exchanges affects arbitrageurs and liquidity providers. Faster blocks weaken priority-fee competition among arbitrageurs and shift rents from the block producer to them. Evidence from Base's Flashblocks upgrade, which increased block speed tenfold, confirms the predictions: priority-fee bids fall sharply and arbitrageurs' net profit rises. Pool depth falls and effective spreads widen.

entry.title: Early detection of rug pulls on Solana, a blockchain, using transaction-graph models.
entry.summary: Early Rug Pull Detection on Solana arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper studies how to flag rug pulls, scams where token creators drain liquidity, on newly launched Solana tokens in their first minutes. The authors analyze 2,700 tokens from SolRPDS using one-minute market data and token transfer graphs. They compare graph neural networks with non-graph models on identical features across observation windows of 12.5, 35.5, and 93 minutes.

entry.title: Splitting Rewards to Stabilize Mining When Only Fees Remain
entry.summary: Splitting for Stability: a Modified Reward Scheme for Transaction-Fee-Only Regimes arXiv · Nov 10, 2026As Bitcoin's block subsidy declines, miner revenue will depend more on transaction fees, which can encourage undercutting and fork-based mining. The paper proposes a reward-splitting scheme in which the winning block producer receives an α portion of the block reward and the rest goes to other miners. Analysis and simulations indicate parameter ranges where honest mining beats fork-based deviations, and the authors report that the scheme does not appear to strengthen selfish mining incentives.

entry.title: Useful Work May Raise Energy Use: Demand Elasticity and Proof of Useful Work
entry.summary: Useful Work Can Increase Energy Use: Demand Elasticity and Proof of Useful Work arXiv · Nov 10, 2026Bitcoin's Proof-of-Work consumes large amounts of electricity, so Proof-of-Useful-Work (PoUW) was proposed to let mining perform useful computations instead. This paper shows that switching to PoUW may increase total electricity consumption, echoing Jevons' paradox. PoUW acts as a subsidy that lowers the effective price of useful work, and if demand is elastic, total consumption rises. The result is proved in a simple model with electricity-only costs.

entry.title: Pastel: Single Secret Leader Election with Private Weights
entry.summary: Pastel: Single Secret Leader Election with Private Weights IACR ePrint · Nov 7, 2026This paper presents Pastel, a single secret leader election (SSLE) protocol in which each party's chance of winning is weighted by its private stake, and the weights remain hidden. It targets proof-of-stake blockchains where stakes are stored encrypted or committed for privacy. The authors concretely implement the zero-knowledge proofs needed for security against malicious adversaries, so the protocol does not rely on slashing for end-to-end malicious security.

entry.title: BioBind: Linking Biometric Deduplication to Zero-Knowledge Authentication
entry.summary: BioBind: Binding Biometric Deduplication to Zero-Knowledge Authentication arXiv · Nov 10, 2026This paper presents BioBind, a protocol for biometric identity credentials in decentralized applications that prevents repeated enrollment and supports private, publicly verifiable authentication. Four backend interface conditions bind the deduplication query, gallery insertion and issued credential to one captured biometric vector and authenticate gallery state transitions. A prototype using LFW face features rejected the tested composition attacks.

entry.title: Agent4Crypto: An LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading with Dual Reflection and Market Feedback
entry.summary: Agent4Crypto: A Dual-Reflective and Market-Feedback-Aligned LLM-Based Multi-Agent System for Cryptocurrency Trading arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper presents Agent4Crypto, a multi-agent system for cryptocurrency trading in which specialized agents handle data collection, analysis, risk assessment, reflection, and trading. Three trader agents with aggressive, neutral, and conservative styles propose actions, and a PPO-based gating policy learns how much weight each trader receives, adjusted through two reflection processes. Experiments on BTC, ETH, and XRP report improved total return and Sharpe ratio compared with traditional, machine learning, reinforcement learning, and existing LLM-based trading baselines.

entry.title: DeFSM: A decentralized, Byzantine-robust way to run federated submodular maximization
entry.summary: DeFSM: Robust and Efficient Decentralization of Federated Submodular Maximization arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper addresses federated submodular maximization, where a central server is a single point of failure and some clients may be Byzantine (malicious). It proposes DeFSM, which replaces the server with a lightweight smart contract and a pool of consensus-free independent agents. Its aggregation rule, SafeGM, uses Tukey depth and safe points from combinatorial geometry to make robust decisions on 2D Gaussian random projections, then lifts them back to convex combinations of actual updates. On CIFAR10 and PathMNIST with up to 30% Byzantine clients and agents, DeFSM never collapses and retains about 91% of the ideal reference quality on average.

entry.title: A quantum-resistant, decentralized notary scheme for blockchain interoperability with a dynamic trust model
entry.summary: A Decentralized Quantum-Resistant Notary Scheme for Blockchain Interoperability with a Novel Dynamic Trust Model arXiv · Nov 9, 2026The paper addresses two weaknesses of existing blockchain notary schemes: vulnerability to quantum attacks and rigid trust management. It proposes a decentralized framework combining ML-KEM, ML-DSA and AES-256, using asymmetric cryptography for authentication and symmetric encryption for bulk data. Under parallel loads of up to 270 transactions per second, the end-to-end performance gap with elliptic-curve approaches averages under 6%. A dynamic trust model derives an adaptive discount factor from the variance of a Verifier's behavior using Popoviciu's inequality, and was evaluated over 200 epochs under adversarial conditions.

entry.title: Verifiable, privacy-preserving collaborative multi-objective optimization on blockchain (zk-NSGA-II)
entry.summary: Verifiable, Privacy-Preserving and Collaborative Multi-Objective Optimization with NSGA-II on Blockchain arXiv · Nov 9, 2026This paper proposes zk-NSGA-II, a protocol that runs NSGA-II on the RISC Zero zkVM so that each evolutionary generation is certified by a succinct proof verified on-chain. Solvers keep private off-chain populations and contribute non-dominated solutions to a shared on-chain Pareto front, with hash chains linking generations to prevent fabricated contributions. The protocol is evaluated on twelve ZDT and DTLZ benchmark problems and a Hang Seng dataset portfolio optimization case study across nine metrics. The results indicate that trustless collaborative multi-objective optimization is feasible with current zero-knowledge and blockchain technologies.

entry.title: Ethereum phishing detection: testing whether extra account-interaction statistics help
entry.summary: Beyond Node Attributes: A Controlled Evaluation and Ablation of Local Interaction Statistics for Ethereum Phishing Detection arXiv · Nov 8, 2026This paper proposes Unlabeled Feature Extension (UFE), 12 local statistics computed from each Ethereum account's incoming and outgoing call and transfer edges without using class labels. UFE is added to the 14 source features of HEIG-Phish and tested with six model families under matched controlled comparisons. Across 20 stratified partitions, UFE raised test Macro-F1 by 1.0 to 9.1 percentage points. An ablation associates most of the gain with the incoming transfer-edge sum attribute.

entry.title: M3FT: A micro-macro-micro reasoning framework for multi-agent crypto perpetual futures trading
entry.summary: M3FT: Micro-Macro-Micro Reasoning for Multi-Agent Cryptocurrency Perpetual Futures Trading arXiv · Nov 7, 2026The paper proposes M3FT, a framework for multi-agent trading of cryptocurrency perpetual futures. Deterministic processing first turns exchange and account data into time-aligned numerical states, which are then converted into explicit market interpretations. Four asset teams refine these through experience retrieval, cross-asset communication and joint-position risk review, and the final stage learns continuous target positions from language and numerical states. On real data, the best configuration achieves a higher mean test return than the evaluated direct LLM, numerical RL and rule-based baselines.

entry.title: Replication certificates: a signed, publication-time record that anyone can verify quickly and later
entry.summary: Replication Certification at Publication: Checkable by Anyone, Anywhere, in Seconds, Forever arXiv · Nov 6, 2026The paper introduces a replication certificate, a cryptographically signed record of deposited data and code files and their logged output. The author reruns the analysis once under a random seed the archive derives from the deposit's hash and a blockchain block, and the archive signs and timestamps the record without rerunning anything. Journals only need to check for the certificate, and anyone can verify or replay each step decades later.

entry.title: Strategic Analysis of Autonomous Scambaiting Agents in Fraud Countermeasures
entry.summary: The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting arXiv · Nov 6, 2026This paper presents a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud, in which autonomous scamming agents and defensive scambaiting agents compete over each other's resources. It analyzes how engagement, resource consumption, belief adaptation, and disruption outcomes evolve over time. The authors report that scammer profitability becomes negative once baiting-agent prevalence exceeds certain thresholds. Under their baseline parameters, when both sides improve at the same rate, the defender's investment in mimicry quality gains more than equivalent scammer investment in detection, so the arms race favors the defender.

entry.title: Post-quantum authentication of IoT data on Ethereum: signature costs and device-signed Merkle roots
entry.summary: Post-Quantum Authentication of IoT Data on Ethereum: Signatures, the Calldata Floor, and Device-Signed Merkle Roots arXiv · Nov 5, 2026This paper measures the cost of adding post-quantum (PQ) authentication to IoT data anchored on Ethereum, under current execution rules including the EIP-7623 calldata floor and EIP-7825 transaction cap, and the calldata repricing planned for Glamsterdam. It evaluates device-side performance of ML-DSA, Falcon, SLH-DSA, LMS and XMSS, reproduces Solidity verifier costs, and introduces a standard-compliant LMS/HSS verifier. Signing every record costs 8.7 times as much as ECDSA even with an ML-DSA precompile, while device-signed Merkle roots over 100 records cost about 3,350 gas per record with LMS versus 245 gas for ECDSA.
